This is an application under Section 5 of Limitation Act, 1963 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for condonation of delay in filing the captioned appeal.
2. Heard and perused the contents of the application 3.
For the sufficient cause being shown in the application, the delay of 91 days in filing the captioned appeal is condoned.
4. The application is disposed of.
MAC.APP. 217/2024 & CM APPL. 24219/2024 (Stay)

1. The instant appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed on behalf of the appellant seeking the following relief:-
"i) Set aside the award passed by the Ld. Trial Court on 20 th September, 2023 and order dated 25th January, 2024 passed against the Appellant further allow the Appellant to put forth his defense and the matter be proceeded with and decide This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of appellant submitted that by way of the application bearing CM APPL. No.24219/2024, the appellant seeks interim relief of stay on the operation of the impugned awards dated 20th September, 2023 and 25th January, 2024.
It is submitted that serious prejudice would be caused to the appellant in case the stay of the operation of the impugned awards is not granted.

On instructions, learned counsel for the appellant undertakes that the appellant shall deposit the entire compensation amount awarded by the learned Tribunal, along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition filed before the learned Tribunal, before the Registrar General of this Court.
It is further submitted that Rs.25,000/- out of the compensation amount has already been paid.
Hence, he prays for grant of interim relief of stay on the operation of the impugned awards.

3. Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant.
4.
Issue notice.
Notice is accepted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent.

5. In regard to the prayer of the appellant with respect to the interim relief, this Court is of the view that the instant matter requires consideration and, prima facie, the balance of convenience lies in favour of the appellant.

6. Therefore, subject to the deposition of the entire compensation amount (excluding Rs.25,000/-
which is already paid) awarded by the learned Tribunal, alongwith interest from the date of filing of the claim petition, before the Registrar General of this Court within four weeks from today, the operation of the impugned awards dated 20th September, 2023 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/08/2024 at 02:18:29 and 25th January, 2024 shall be kept in abeyance till the next date of hearing.
The amount so deposited by the appellant shall be invested in an interest bearing FDR in an auto renewal mode.
7. List on 22nd October, 2024.
CHANDRA DHARI SINGH, J AUGUST 13, 2024 Dy/aa
